question: Why does Lassa fever spike during the dry season?

question: Why would a doctor choose an MRI over a standard X-ray for a patient?

question: Why must nurses avoid gastric aspiration in a patient who swallowed strong caustic lye?

question: Why is carbidopa combined with levodopa when treating Parkinson's disease?

question: What is the main purpose of doing a FAST scan at the bedside of an emergency trauma patient?

options.A: To count the precise number of broken ribs in the chest wall

question: When is it legally and ethically okay for a nurse to share a patient's confidential abuse details?

question: What is the primary underlying cause of coronary artery disease?

question: Why is it so important to check lab results alongside a physical assessment rather than trusting the numbers alone?

options.C: Because clinical symptoms show how the patient is tolerating the physiological shift

question: What actually happens in the body during endometriosis?

question: Why does pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) raise a woman's risk of having an ectopic pregnancy?

options.C: Infection prevents the ovaries from releasing eggs
options.D: Bacteria destroy the muscular walls of the uterus

question: What do we mean when we say an ultrasound is 'operator-dependent'?

options.C: Patients must pay a separate fee every time the probe touches their skin

question: Why does the electrical signal pause briefly at the AV node before heading down to the ventricles?

question: What do we call any environmental factor or substance that causes birth defects in an unborn baby?

question: When does a polyvalent nurse need critical thinking the most?

question: What is the absolute top nursing priority when caring for someone with a severe upper airway problem?

question: Which external structure is a small, highly sensitive erectile organ?

question: What should you do if you notice sudden joint swelling and severe redness during an exercise session?

question: What is the primary role of the Reticular Activating System (RAS) in the brain stem?

options.A: Processing visual images from the eyes

options.D: Regulating resting heart rate

question: Which body receptor is mainly responsible for the pain-relieving power of strong opioids?

options.A: Alpha receptor
options.B: Mu receptor
options.C: Beta receptor

explanation: The mu receptor is the main target for opioids to kill pain, though it's also why strong opioids can cause drowsiness and slow breathing. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T1#GNS223_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why should a nurse avoid raising the legs of a patient experiencing cardiogenic shock?

question: During a reproductive review of systems, which symptom is a red flag that needs a closer look?

question: What is the main difference between an 'adolescent' and 'adolescence'?

question: Why does a patient continue to experience monthly menstrual periods after getting her tubes tied?

question: How can a nurse prevent reading errors (parallax errors) when using a weighing scale?

question: Why do we ask a female patient to empty her bladder right before a pelvic examination?

question: What is a major duty of a healthcare social worker?

question: A patient with a severe bone infection is losing weight rapidly despite resting in bed all day. What is the main reason for this?

question: How do daily community health records help with national health planning in Nigeria?

question: In a busy emergency unit, why do nurses grab the glucometer so quickly?

question: What is the main health benefit of early breast milk (colostrum) for a newborn?

question: What is the main purpose of using the teach-back method?

options.B: To confirm whether the patient truly understands the instructions
options.C: To give the nurse a break from talking
options.D: To test the patient's long-term memory capacity

explanation: Correct! Asking them to explain it back in their own words is the best way to make sure they got the right message. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h6)

question: How does benzonatate work to stop a patient's cough?

options.A: Anesthetizing stretch receptors in the respiratory tract
options.B: Depressing the heart rate to lower blood pressure
options.C: Paralyzing the muscles of the abdominal wall
options.D: Blocking histamine receptors in the nasal passages

explanation: Benzonatate acts locally by gently numbing the stretch receptors in the airways, stopping the urge to cough right at the source. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T1#GNS223_U2_T1_h2)

question: What happens in the body when a drug reaches 'steady-state' during regular dosing?

options.A: The drug stops working because the liver destroys all remaining molecules
options.B: The rate of drug intake equals the rate of drug elimination
options.C: The concentration in the blood continues to climb infinitely
options.D: Absorption drops to zero while excretion speeds up rapidly

explanation: Steady-state is a sweet spot! It means the amount of drug you take in matches the amount your body clears out, keeping your therapeutic blood levels nice and stable. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the best reason to place a healthy newborn skin-to-skin on mum's chest right after birth?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need to dry the baby with warm towels
options.B: It allows the nurse to perform the complete physical head-to-toe exam faster
options.C: It prevents the infant from passing meconium before the placenta is delivered
options.D: It helps maintain the newborn's body temperature and encourages early breastfeeding

explanation: Mum's chest is like a natural incubator! Skin-to-skin keeps baby warm and wakes up those natural instincts to latch and breastfeed. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h5)

question: When checking a patient with dark skin for inflammation, what should you look out for?

options.A: Dark brown, purplish, or grey discoloration instead of bright redness
options.B: Bright cherry-red patches that are easily visible on all skin types
options.C: Neon yellow borders surrounding every single affected skin plaque
options.D: A complete absence of any color change with only flaking present

explanation: Great clinical eye! On darker skin tones, inflammation often shows up as deeper brown, purple, or grey shades rather than standard red. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is the correct needle insertion angle for an intradermal injection?

options.A: 5 to 15 degrees
options.B: 60 to 75 degrees
options.C: 90 degrees
options.D: 45 degrees

explanation: A very shallow angle of 5 to 15 degrees keeps the needle in the superficial dermal layer instead of slipping deeper. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is widely considered the gold standard of psychological treatment for ICT addiction?

options.A: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy
options.B: Strict physical punishment
options.C: Electroconvulsive therapy
options.D: Total isolation from society

explanation: CBT (the approach behind this app!) helps patients spot unhelpful thought patterns and build practical coping skills to manage their screen habits. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h7)

question: Which bar chart style places sub-category bars directly on top of each other to show a total?

options.A: Grouped bar chart
options.B: Stacked bar chart
options.C: Simple bar chart
options.D: Scatter plot chart

explanation: A stacked bar chart segments a single bar to show both individual parts and the combined total. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h3)

question: A patient actively moves their arm through space without any nurse assistance. What type of movement is being tested?

options.A: Resisted range of motion
options.B: Reflexive range of motion
options.C: Active range of motion
options.D: Passive range of motion

explanation: Active range of motion occurs when the patient moves the joint entirely on their own power without outside assistance. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h2)

question: What happens when you mix ordinary trash with infectious medical waste?

options.A: The entire batch becomes dangerous infectious waste
options.B: The total volume of waste decreases significantly
options.C: The waste can be safely recycled as normal trash
options.D: The infectious waste automatically becomes harmless

explanation: You've got this! Mixing clean trash with infectious material contaminates everything, which drives up disposal costs and safety risks. Always segregate early! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which needle gauge is best for a routine subcutaneous injection?

options.A: 32 to 36 gauge
options.B: 20 to 22 gauge
options.C: 25 to 30 gauge
options.D: 14 to 18 gauge

explanation: Higher gauge numbers mean thinner needles! A 25 to 30 gauge needle slips in smoothly and keeps the injection as painless as possible. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which common side effect of oral iron often scares patients, even though it's harmless?

options.A: Temporary hair thinning
options.B: Excessive saliva production
options.C: Bright yellow urine coloration
options.D: Dark or black-colored stools

explanation: Don't panic your patients! Unabsorbed iron turns stools dark or black, and it's a totally normal, harmless side effect. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T6#GNS223_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is recording past medical and surgical history important during an admission assessment?

options.A: It replaces the need to ask about current medications
options.B: It predicts the exact date the patient will be discharged
options.C: It proves the patient has visited a hospital before
options.D: It helps identify chronic conditions that may affect current treatment

explanation: Knowing past health problems helps the healthcare team anticipate complications and tailor current therapy safely. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which maneuver should you use to open the airway of a patient with a suspected neck injury?

options.A: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.B: Neck-hyperextension method
options.C: Lateral recovery position
options.D: Head-tilt, chin-lift maneuver

explanation: When a neck injury is suspected, use the jaw-thrust maneuver. It opens the airway gently without bending the vulnerable cervical spine. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is an effective way to help prevent puerperal sepsis during labor?

options.A: Delaying bladder emptying until after delivery
options.B: Encouraging strict bed rest for the entire duration of labor
options.C: Limiting the number of unnecessary vaginal examinations
options.D: Avoiding all routine perineal hygiene measures

explanation: Every vaginal exam is a chance to introduce bacteria. Doing only necessary exams helps keep the birth canal safer from outside germs. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h8)
